MC: Topic 01 — Information Architecture & Responsive Wireframing | Q01 — Content inventory
A redesign has 46 pages, including duplicates and obsolete notices. What should precede a new navigation hierarchy?

column3: Create a visual style guide
Audit content for purpose, audience, ownership and disposition
Design desktop navigation first
Remove every page with low traffic

MC: Correct answer: B. A content inventory and audit identify what should be kept, revised, merged or removed before organizing the site.
MC
Topic 01 — Information Architecture & Responsive Wireframing | Q02 — Navigation labels
In a usability test, visitors repeatedly overlook a link labelled “Opportunities” when seeking tuition assistance. What is the strongest IA revision?

column3: Increase its font size without changing the label
Replace it with a descriptive label such as “Financial Aid” and retest
Move it into the footer
Use an icon without text

MC: Correct answer: B. Navigation labels should match users’ vocabulary and predict destination content; a descriptive label reduces ambiguity.
MC
Topic 01 — Information Architecture & Responsive Wireframing | Q03 — Hierarchy versus URL
A sitemap groups “Apply,” “Tuition,” and “Programs” under “Admissions.” What does this primarily represent?

column3: The mandatory server folder structure
An information hierarchy and navigational relationship
A CSS component dependency graph
The final database schema

MC: Correct answer: B. A sitemap communicates conceptual content hierarchy; it need not dictate physical URL or server folder organization.
MC
Topic 01 — Information Architecture & Responsive Wireframing | Q04 — Journey failure
A prospective student can reach an application form only after opening seven unrelated pages. Which evidence best supports restructuring?

column3: The number of fonts on the homepage
A task walkthrough showing unnecessary navigation steps
The homepage image resolution
The website framework version

MC: Correct answer: B. A task walkthrough traces the user goal and exposes friction in the navigation path.
MC
Topic 01 — Information Architecture & Responsive Wireframing | Q05 — Sitemap completeness
A sitemap includes “Services” but none of its distinct destinations. What is the main problem for evaluating navigation?

column3: It uses a category label
It conceals the intended information destinations and their relationships
It does not specify colour values
It lacks animation timing

MC: Correct answer: B. Without destinations, reviewers cannot judge whether the information structure supports user tasks.
MC
Topic 01 — Information Architecture & Responsive Wireframing | Q06 — Content priority
On a mobile wireframe for an emergency campus closure, which content should be most prominent?

column3: A decorative campus image
The closure status and immediate instructions
A full archive of historical notices
A social media feed

MC: Correct answer: B. High-priority, time-sensitive tasks should lead the content hierarchy, especially with limited screen space.
MC
Topic 02 — Responsive UI Design & Figma Prototyping | Q07 — Low fidelity
Why should a team validate low-fidelity wireframes before creating polished screens?

column3: Wireframes guarantee accessibility
They expose layout and task-flow problems before visual polish becomes costly
They replace all user testing
They establish production CSS automatically

MC: Correct answer: B. Early low-fidelity validation makes structural revisions inexpensive and prevents visual detail from obscuring flow problems.
MC
Topic 02 — Responsive UI Design & Figma Prototyping | Q08 — Responsive adaptation
A desktop layout has a three-column card grid. What is the most defensible mobile-first approach?

column3: Keep three columns at every width
Start with a readable single column and expand when space permits
Hide two-thirds of the cards on phones
Scale the entire desktop canvas down

MC: Correct answer: B. Responsive design adapts layout to available space while retaining access to meaningful content.
MC
Topic 02 — Responsive UI Design & Figma Prototyping | Q09 — Breakpoint decision
What is the best reason to introduce a responsive breakpoint?

column3: A device brand has a new model
The layout or content begins to fail at a particular width
Every 100 pixels requires a breakpoint
The design tool offers preset frame names

MC: Correct answer: B. Breakpoints should respond to content and layout needs rather than arbitrary device labels.
MC
Topic 02 — Responsive UI Design & Figma Prototyping | Q10 — Wireframe annotation
A desktop navigation becomes a menu button on mobile. What annotation best supports handoff?

column3: “Make mobile better”
Describe trigger, expanded state, keyboard access and navigation behavior
Specify only the icon colour
List the designer’s favourite menu patterns

MC: Correct answer: B. Behavioral annotations clarify interaction and accessibility expectations beyond static screenshots.
MC
Topic 02 — Responsive UI Design & Figma Prototyping | Q11 — Task flow
A wireframe shows a “Register” button but no confirmation or error state. What is missing?

column3: A larger heading
A complete task flow with system feedback
A second accent colour
A grid overlay

MC: Correct answer: B. A task flow must include outcome and error feedback, not merely the initiating action.
MC
Topic 02 — Responsive UI Design & Figma Prototyping | Q12 — Figma variants
A component has default, hover, focus and disabled variants. What is the primary benefit?

column3: It guarantees correct HTML semantics
It documents consistent interactive states for implementation
It eliminates responsive testing
It makes every state keyboard-accessible automatically

MC: Correct answer: B. Component variants communicate intended visual and interaction states consistently; code and testing are still required.
MC
Topic 02 — Responsive UI Design & Figma Prototyping | Q13 — Prototype limitations
A clickable Figma prototype successfully demonstrates navigation. What claim is NOT justified by that result alone?

column3: The intended screen sequence is represented
The navigation can be reviewed with participants
The deployed HTML site meets keyboard accessibility requirements
The prototype supports early flow testing

MC: Correct answer: C. Figma interactions do not prove that production HTML semantics, keyboard behavior or accessibility are correct.
MC
Topic 03 — Design-to-Code & Responsive Implementation | Q14 — Semantic controls
A design shows a control that submits a form. Which HTML element is most appropriate?

column3: A clickable div with no keyboard handling
A button with type="submit"
A span with a pointer cursor
An anchor without an href

MC: Correct answer: B. A submit button provides native semantics, keyboard activation and form submission behavior.
MC
Topic 03 — Design-to-Code & Responsive Implementation | Q15 — CSS tokens
A site uses the same accent colour in 18 components. What implementation most improves maintainability?

column3: Repeat the hex value in every selector
Define a CSS custom property and reference it consistently
Use inline styles on each element
Convert every component into an image

MC: Correct answer: B. A shared CSS custom property centralizes a design decision and makes coordinated changes easier.
MC
Topic 03 — Design-to-Code & Responsive Implementation | Q16 — Flex versus grid
A header has a logo, navigation group and utility actions arranged along one main axis. Which CSS tool is the best default?

column3: Flexbox
CSS columns
Absolute positioning for every child
A background image

MC: Correct answer: A. Flexbox is well suited to one-dimensional alignment and distribution of header groups.
MC
Topic 03 — Design-to-Code & Responsive Implementation | Q17 — Responsive grid
A card collection should automatically fit as many readable columns as available, with each card at least 16rem wide when possible. Which CSS is most suitable?

column3: grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(16rem, 1fr))
grid-template-columns: repeat(6, 1fr)
position: absolute on every card
width: 16rem on the entire grid

MC: Correct answer: A. Auto-fit with minmax allows responsive column counts while maintaining a practical minimum card width.
MC
Topic 03 — Design-to-Code & Responsive Implementation | Q18 — Mobile overflow
A 375px viewport displays a horizontal scrollbar after adding a hero image. What should be investigated first?

column3: Whether an element or fixed width exceeds its container
Whether the body font is serif
Whether the page has too few headings
Whether the browser tab has a favicon

MC: Correct answer: A. Horizontal overflow often results from fixed widths, oversized media or unbreakable content; inspect the offending element.
MC
Topic 03 — Design-to-Code & Responsive Implementation | Q19 — Figma fidelity
A Figma button uses a 12px radius and 16px horizontal padding, but the coded version differs. What is the best corrective workflow?

column3: Adjust random values until it looks acceptable
Inspect the design specifications, map them to reusable CSS tokens and compare states
Export the button as a bitmap
Remove the Figma component

MC: Correct answer: B. A disciplined design-to-code workflow traces visual decisions to reusable implementation values and verifies the result.
MC
Topic 03 — Design-to-Code & Responsive Implementation | Q20 — Deployment distinction
A student pushes HTML/CSS to GitHub, but the project has no public URL. Which statement is accurate?

column3: GitHub automatically proves the site is deployed
The repository stores source; GitHub Pages must be configured and verified for publication
Figma is the deployment host
A README alone makes the site public

MC: Correct answer: B. A GitHub repository and a GitHub Pages deployment serve different purposes; publishing must be enabled and checked.
MC
Topic 04 — Accessibility Audit & Remediation | Q21 — Keyboard focus
A custom navigation menu opens on mouse hover but not by keyboard. What is the most important remediation?

column3: Increase the hover animation duration
Implement keyboard-operable controls and visible focus indication
Replace text labels with icons
Add a larger background image

MC: Correct answer: B. Keyboard users need operable controls, focus visibility and a way to open and close the menu.
MC
Topic 04 — Accessibility Audit & Remediation | Q22 — Contrast scope
A primary button passes text contrast, but its focus indicator blends into the background. What follows?

column3: The button is fully accessible because text contrast passes
The focus indicator requires separate visibility and contrast evaluation
Focus indicators are optional for keyboard users
Changing font weight fixes focus visibility

MC: Correct answer: B. Readable text does not establish that keyboard focus is perceivable; the focus indicator must also be assessed.
MC
Topic 04 — Accessibility Audit & Remediation | Q23 — Alternative text
A decorative wave graphic appears next to a heading and conveys no information. What is the appropriate image treatment?

column3: Use alt text repeating the heading
Use an empty alt attribute so assistive technology can skip it
Use the file name as alt text
Remove the heading and rely on the image

MC: Correct answer: B. Purely decorative images should normally have empty alternative text to avoid redundant announcements.
MC
Topic 04 — Accessibility Audit & Remediation | Q24 — Form error
A required email field fails validation. Which feedback most supports accessible recovery?

column3: Show a red border only
Provide a specific text error linked to the field and preserve entered data
Clear the entire form
Display “Invalid” in an unrelated footer

MC: Correct answer: B. Errors should be communicated in text, associated with the relevant input and help users correct the issue.
MC
Topic 04 — Accessibility Audit & Remediation | Q25 — Audit evidence
An accessibility audit reports “keyboard navigation is broken.” What evidence makes the finding actionable?

column3: A screenshot of the homepage only
Affected control, reproduction steps, expected behavior, observed behavior and proposed fix
The developer’s preferred browser
A general recommendation to improve accessibility

MC: Correct answer: B. Actionable audit findings identify a reproducible issue and a verifiable remediation path.
